messages.author: 04e62c3b36bb17bf
messages.subject: Multiple QTL modelling in R/qtl2
parts:
Hi Karl, 
I am trying to do some multiple QTL modelling in R/qtl2. Not necessarily as complex as qtl::stepwiseqtl, but more along the lines of addqtl and refineqtl. Is there functionality for this type of thing in qtl2? 
I have some code to do something akin to qtl::refineqtl ... I build covariate matrices out of the maxarg for each of the scan1 QTL peaks, then run subsequent QTL scans iteratively with all but one of the QTL maxarg matrices as covariates. Would you recommend using this approach, or do think it might violate some of the assumptions of the scan1 model. 
Any advice is appreciated. 
Thanks,
John

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Multiple QTL modelling in R/qtl2
parts:
There's nothing of this sort yet in R/qtl2.

I would avoid using maxmarg() and would instead use the genotype probabilities themselves.

karl

messages.author: 04e62c3b36bb17bf
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Multiple QTL modelling in R/qtl2
parts:
Thanks again Karl, 
A follow up question: now that I have built out an additive (no epistasis) multiple QTL model, I'd like to calculate the percent variance explained for each significant locus. What method would you suggest to do this? I was thinking about including the genotype probabilities of the full model (probs for each QTL cbind'd together) as the addcovar, then running est_herit and iteratively dropping columns in addcovar associated with each QTL. PVE would then be the difference in the polygenic heritability between the model with and without each QTL. 
Would this approach be appropriate, or should I just transform the LOD scores?
Thanks,
John

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Multiple QTL modelling in R/qtl2
parts:
Rather than use est_herit as your describe, I'd be more inclined to
transform LOD scores.
Provided you have no linked QTL, I'd compare the variance of the
residuals with and without a particular QTL in the model, but I think
this translates directly to the LOD score.

I think ideally one would use the estimated coefficients under the
fitted multiple-QTL model, but I'm not entirely sure how to do it.

karl

messages.author: bccf789db78f8994
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Multiple QTL modelling in R/qtl2
parts: Hi there-- I'm trying to follow the conversation here but want to check my understanding-- PVE is percent variance explained? And the output from making that transformation is similar to comparing the variance of the phenotype residuals with and without a particular QTL-- because the same information goes into calculating the LOD score? Thanks for your time!
On Tuesday, August 27, 2019 at 9:53:07 AM UTC-5, Karl Broman wrote:

Rather than use est_herit as your describe, I'd be more inclined to
transform LOD scores.
Provided you have no linked QTL, I'd compare the variance of the
residuals with and without a particular QTL in the model, but I think
this translates directly to the LOD score.

I think ideally one would use the estimated coefficients under the
fitted multiple-QTL model, but I'm not entirely sure how to do it.

karl

On 8/27/19 7:33 AM, John Lovell wrote:
> Thanks again Karl,
> A follow up question: now that I have built out an additive (no
> epistasis) multiple QTL model, I'd like to calculate the percent
> variance explained for each significant locus. What method would you
> suggest to do this? I was thinking about including the genotype
> probabilities of the full model (probs for each QTL cbind'd together)
> as the addcovar, then running est_herit and iteratively dropping
> columns in addcovar associated with each QTL. PVE would then be the
> difference in the polygenic heritability between the model with and
> without each QTL.
> Would this approach be appropriate, or should I just transform the LOD
> scores?
> Thanks,
> John
>
> On Friday, August 16, 2019 at 9:28:27 AM UTC-6, Karl Broman wrote:
>
>     I've definitely seen cases where conditioning on the genotype
>     probabilities doesn't get rid of the signal. Sometimes sampling
>     from the probabilities (a single imputation) helps.
>
>     karl
>
>     > On Aug 16, 2019, at 10:18 AM, John Lovell <> wrote:
>     >
>     > OK - cool. Yeah, I was seeing some residual signal when using
>     maxarg(), the LOD goes to 0 when I use genoprobs. Thanks.
>     > John
>     >
>     >
>     > On Friday, August 16, 2019 at 11:10:04 AM UTC-4, Karl Broman wrote:
>     > There's nothing of this sort yet in R/qtl2.
>     >
>     > I would avoid using maxmarg() and would instead use the genotype
>     probabilities themselves.
>     >
>     > karl
>     >
>     >
>     > >
>     > > Hi Karl,
>     > > I am trying to do some multiple QTL modelling in R/qtl2. Not
>     necessarily as complex as qtl::stepwiseqtl, but more along the
>     lines of addqtl and refineqtl. Is there functionality for this
>     type of thing in qtl2?
>     > > I have some code to do something akin to qtl::refineqtl ... I
>     build covariate matrices out of the maxarg for each of the scan1
>     QTL peaks, then run subsequent QTL scans iteratively with all but
>     one of the QTL maxarg matrices as covariates. Would you recommend
>     using this approach, or do think it might violate some of the
>     assumptions of the scan1 model.
>     > > Any advice is appreciated.
>     > > Thanks,
>     > > John

Yes, that's right. It's describe in the R/qtl book on page 77.
It's an approximation that assumes complete genotype data at the putative QTL.

karl
